purpose: Presentation copy only. Nothing here changes a probability, a coefficient or a ranking. It renames and explains factors that already exist, so a salesperson can read them.
label_contract: `label` is the ONE LINE the lead card prints. It must answer 'why did this factor move the score' on its own, with no tooltip and no second field. Shape: '<what was observed> - <why that matters>'. It replaces the old technical names ('Lead locale'), which named the input instead of giving the reason.
non_causal_rule: Every sentence describes an ASSOCIATION observed in training data. Never 'caused', 'because', 'due to', 'drives' or 'makes'. A logistic coefficient is not a cause.
comparison_note: Categorical factors are scored against a reference level, so their wording is comparative on purpose: seniority against an individual contributor, email against Gmail, locale against India. 'Converts above Gmail' is the literal meaning of the coefficient - do not reword it into an absolute claim.

summary.purpose: Copy for the narrative summary: two or three plain sentences answering 'why are we showing this purchase probability for this lead'. Assembled from factors that already exist; it introduces no number the response does not already carry.
summary.style_rule: Written for a salesperson. No log-odds, coefficients, contributions, percentiles, deciles or internal field names. Supportive verbs only - a signal 'supports', 'helps' or 'holds back' a probability; it never causes a purchase and the lead never 'will buy'.

templates.opening: This lead has a {percent}% purchase probability because {positives}.
templates.opening_no_positives: This lead has a {percent}% purchase probability.
templates.positives_only: Together these signals put the probability {standing}.
templates.positives_only_no_base: Together these signals point to stronger intent than the average lead.
templates.no_factors: This lead has a {percent}% purchase probability. No single signal stood out strongly enough to highlight.
templates.unscorable: There is not enough point-in-time information about this lead to give it a purchase probability.
templates.positives_only_one_no_base: That signal points to stronger intent than the average lead.

summary.note: Engagement and brand-fit signals describe how well this lead fits the brand. They inform the lead's ranking; the percentage itself comes from the form submission the lead was scored on.
summary.basis: Assembled from the factors listed above. Every number here already appears elsewhere in this response; nothing is recomputed.

clause_contract: `clause` is a sentence fragment for the narrative summary, written as a verb phrase with an implied subject so it reads inside '...because they X, and Y.' The `label` fields are headlines for a card row and do not fit mid-sentence. Same non-causal rule applies: describe what was observed, not what caused a purchase. Keep a clause free of commas: several are joined into one sentence, and internal punctuation makes the list unparseable.
